pages.transcription:
New York, 18.7.40

Dear Manfred,
I have to-day written to Hanna by
ordinary mail, but I hope that this letter
will reach you quicker. We have not had any
letters from you since we are here and I am
anxiously waiting for them. We are after all
not leaving for South America before the 9th Aug,
so you can write us c/o Viking Press and they would
forward by air any letters which arrive after
our departure.
I suppose you got the affidavit which
was sent to you last week for Eva through
Stephen Wise, whose wife is leading in the reception
committee. As soon as I know about the prospects of
Eva's coming I shall get in touch with them to
see where they propose to settle her. In the meantime
I am enquiring about boarding-schools and
among our friends. Anita Bahn from Frankfurt -
Hanna knows her - would take Eva for the be-
ginning, but perhaps I find a better solution
soon. My sister-in-law might also agree to take Eva
for a while but although she will be all-right
for taking her out or for holidays, I would not
recommend the atmosphere for more than a very
short time.
I hope that all of you keep well and
am impatiently looking forward to a letter.
There is so much we want to know about you, your
work, Rosemont, Heines and Marta and I hope you
have written long letters to New York.
Kindest regards, Lotte

[Rand links, vertikal geschrieben:] Kindest regards to Mama, I shall write her to-morrow.
[Rand rechts, vertikal geschrieben:] Kindest regards, Lotte
